reason: Citation is verbatim: NodeListener.java:172 is `@EventHandler(priority = EventPriority.NORMAL)` with no ignoreCancelled, and the only early returns inside onPlayerInteract (lines 174-175 hand/action, 178 null block, 181 non-arena world, 183 non-node block, 191 null PlayerData, 199-206 not-running/settlement) never test event.isCancelled(); a grep for isCancelled/useInteractedBlock/useItemInHand over NodeListener.java returns zero hits, so a pre-cancelled PlayerInteractEvent falls straight through to the repair branch (line 210 `if (isRepairItem(item))`, 234 repairNode, 237-247 setAmount/setItemInMainHand(null)). The class's own convention proves the omission is an oversight, not a decision: lines 103, 114, 124 and 145 all declare `ignoreCancelled = true`, and sibling FireballListener.java:296 shows the manual `if (event.isCancelled()) return;` pattern the author uses when ignoreCancelled is unsuitable. Reachability is real because Bukkit keeps dispatching a cancelled event to handlers that did not opt into ignoreCancelled, so a region/claim/adventure guard that cancels at LOWEST/LOW/NORMAL still sees the node healed and the ghast tear decremented (repair-cost-item: GHAST_TEAR, repair-cost-amount: 1). No in-plugin listener can cancel it first (LobbyProtectionListener.onInteract at line 212 is gated by exempt()->inLobby(), and NodeListener.gm() only matches arena worlds; ArenaAccessListener handles PlayerTeleportEvent only), so the trigger is an added protection plugin/region — an admin-config contingency the protocol says is not a revoke ground, but it does mean the shipped server (only HilltopVillage + Let's Learn English installed) does not exhibit it today. The finding's ordering claim is even understated: a canceller running after NORMAL (e.g. HIGHEST) leaves the same outcome, since the repair has already been applied by then.
